newsitem.title: USA: MARINO OUT INDEFINITELY WITH FRACTURED ANKLE.
newsitem.headline: MARINO OUT INDEFINITELY WITH FRACTURED ANKLE.

text.p: MIAMI, Sept 24 - Miami Dolphins star quarterback Dan Marino has a fractured right ankle and is out indefinitely, the National Football League club said Tuesday.

Marino left Monday night's 10-6 loss at Indianapolis in the first quarter with an ankle injury and did not return. X-rays taken at the stadium and the injury originally was diagnosed as a sprain. But an MRI Tuesday revealed a non-displaced fracture.

"The MRI test taken today showed an acute non-displaced fracture of his (right ankle)," Dolphins trainer Kevin O'Neill said in a statement. "Proper steps are being taken to stabilise the fracture, and he will begin a course of treatment and rehabilitation."
O'Neill gave no timetable as to Marino's possible return.
Head coach Jimmy Johnson, however, held out hope in his weekly news conference Tuesday, saying that without complications Marino would miss the next three to four weeks.
The Dolphins (3-1) have a bye week before hosting the Seattle Seahawks Oct. 6.

The 35-year-old Marino was limping slightly as he came off the field following Miami's first possession. He completed 5-of-6 passes to move the Dolphins to the Colts 7-yard line before throwing two incompletions in the end zone.

Marino removed his shoe and was treated on the sideline by trainers, who wrapped his foot in tape and administered an ice pack. He stayed on the sidelines until late in the first half, when he was taken to the locker room on a golf cart.
Veteran Bernie Kosar replaced Marino. Craig Erickson, who played for coach Johnson at the University of Miami and was signed early in the season, is the third-stringer.
